problem: Find an equation of the plane that contains the point  $Q(3,2,0)$ and is  perpendicular to the vector $n=⟨1,-2,5⟩.$
worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of $Q$ is $q=⟨3,2,0⟩,$ and $n=⟨1,-2,5⟩$ is normal to the plane.

The equation of the plane that passes though the point $Q({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ and is perpendicular to the vector $n$ can be given as

$$
(r-q)\cdot n=0,
$$

where $r$ is the position vector of any point on the plane, and $q$ is the position vector of $Q.$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-q)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n-q\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =q\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨1,-2,5⟩ & =⟨3,2,0⟩\cdot ⟨1,-2,5⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨1,-2,5⟩ & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$
